title: Two-bedroom flats in Jaysburg

paragraphs.text: Section one.
You will hear a woman phoning an estate agent about renting a flat in a city called Jaysburg.
First, you have some time to look at questions one to six on page two.
You will see that there is an example that has been done for you. On this occasion only, the conversation relating to this will be played first.
Hello, Key Data Estate Agency.
Hi. My name's Susie Beck. I'm looking for a two-bedroom flat to rent in Jaysburg.
Okay. And which area are you looking in, Ms. Beck?
Low Town.
Let me just look.
Okay, I've got three here which might be suitable. First, there's number fifty-seven, Prince's Square, Low Town.
Right.
The address of the flat is fifty-seven Prince's Square, Low Town, so fifty-seven has been written in the space.
Now we shall begin.
You should answer the questions as you listen because you will not hear the recording a second time.
Listen carefully and answer questions one to six.
Hello, Key Data Estate Agency.
Hi. My name's Susie Beck. I'm looking for a two-bedroom flat to rent in Jaysburg.
Okay. And which area are you looking in, Ms. Beck?
Low Town.
Let me just look.
Okay, I've got three here which might be suitable. First, there's number fifty-seven, Prince's Square, Low Town.
Right.
As well as the two good-sized bedrooms, it's got a bathroom, sitting room, and a kitchen. And there's a dining area in the kitchen.
That's good. I don't like kitchens that are too small. What about outside? Ideally, I'd like a bit of a garden.
Yes, there's a shared one, but it hasn't got a parking space, I'm afraid. That shouldn't be a problem, though. It's a nice, quiet area. You can just leave your car on the street.
Okay. How much is it?
It's 1200 pounds a month, and it's available from the 28th of August, next Monday.
Okay. What's the second flat like?
It's in Green Park.
Green Park? Is that still in Low Town?
No, actually, it's not. It's just outside to the north of there.
So that's Northgate, isn't it?
That's right.
Oh. That's okay.
So the rooms in that one, it's got a nice sized bathroom, kitchen, sitting room, and there's also a balcony leading out from the sitting room. It's not big, but it looks very nice in the photos.
Right. And outside?
Just a garage.
Okay. And what rent are they asking?
1250 pounds.

If you're interested in that one, it's not available right now. The present lease ends in the middle of September, but then we inspect it and leave time for repairs and so on. So that means it'll be free to move into on the 13th of September. Would that be okay for you?
Yes, that would be fine.
Now, the third one's in New Quayside, Low Town.
Oh? I have a friend who used to live there. They're nice flats.
Yes. Aren't they? So you know the basic layout of the flat?
Yes. Ultra-modern bathroom and kitchen, big sitting room. And then you get the use of a gym, don't you?
That's right. But no swimming pool, unfortunately.
Oh, well. A gym's more useful. And what's the rent on that one?

Actually, because the owners really need to find a tenant as soon as possible, they've just agreed to drop the rent a bit. They were asking one thousand four hundred pounds a month, but they'll accept 1375 pounds now.
Okay. So obviously that's available straight away.
Yes.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions seven to ten on page two.
Now listen and answer questions seven to ten.
Right. Well, I'd like to see the flat at New Quayside. Can we fix up a viewing?
Of course. Just one moment while I look at my calendar. Could you do Thursday afternoon?
Uh, I'd prefer Friday, if at all possible.
No, sorry. It'd have to be Thursday or otherwise Monday next week.
Okay, this week. What about the time?
When would suit you?
I'm busy until three, and then I'll need at least half an hour to get there. What about three forty-five? Or later, if you prefer.
No, that's fine.
Shall we meet at the flats?
Uh, will you be driving there? There isn't any on-street parking right near the flats. The residents all have single garages.
Right. But there's a cafe in New Quayside, isn't there? We could meet outside there and leave our cars in the street next to it.
Okay. Do you remember exactly where it is?
Uh, it's at the entrance to New Quayside, isn't it?
That's right.
But can you give me directions to New Quayside from the main roundabout in Low Town? It's ages since I've been there.
Yes. Take the first right turning after that roundabout. Go straight on until you reach a bridge. Turn left there into New Quayside.
Okay. I'll probably remember the way when I get there. And can you tell me your name, please?
Yes, it's Edward. Edward Treloar. That's T-R-E-L-O-A-R.
Thank you. I'll see you at New Quayside then.
Yes, bye.
Bye.
That is the end of section one.
You now have half a minute to check your answers.
